Subject: Vendr profile staging: delegated upload SLA & evidence TTL policy

Hi Ari / Sam,

Thanks for taking the call last week. We ran through Vendr staging during the demo and a couple of items need clarification before Catalyst Health signs off on the profile handoff:

- Delegated upload model: who is responsible for short-lived credentials (temp S3 presign vs service account) and what SLAs do you guarantee for presign availability (100ms vs 500ms)?
- Evidence TTL policy: Catalyst needs an explicit TTL for ephemeral evidence fragments we push to staging (they want a 14-day retention window for temp artifacts, but Vendr documentation references a "default TTL" without a numeric).
- Ownership metadata: we want to ensure proof-of-possession fields (uploader, timestamp, manifest hash) remain immutable in the staging manifest.

I'm attaching a quick evidence_manifest_v1.csv and a proposed delegation_matrix.xlsx for initial review. Can you confirm the presign flow you expect and whether a 14-day TTL is acceptable (or if Vendr enforces a minimum/maximum)?

Marissa — looping you in for procurement record and to flag any contract implications (SLA / data retention).

Next steps: Ari, could you reply with the presign URL pattern, expected token lifetime, and any constraints on manifest fields? If you prefer, we can set up a 30-min tech sync this week.

Thanks,

Ben — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Quick answers inline, then a few clarifying questions: 

1) Presign model and SLA
- Vendr supports two flows: (A) short-lived presign URLs generated via API tokens (recommended for customer-managed uploads), and (B) managed service-account uploads (server-to-server).
- SLA: We aim for 99.9% presign request availability; median generation latency ~120ms in our us-west cluster. We do not currently guarantee 100ms for on-demand presign under heavy burst.
- Token lifetime: configurable; default is 1 hour. We can adjust to 15 minutes for tighter windows if you prefer.

2) Evidence TTL
- By default Vendr retains staging artifacts for 30 days. We can configure tenant-level TTLs between 7 and 90 days. 14 days is supported; we'll add a tenant policy flag to enforce it.

3) Immutable metadata
- We persist uploader, upload_ts (ISO8601), and manifest_sha256. Those fields are recorded as immutable once the object is accepted into staging. We surface them via the Vendor API and the manifest export.

Questions for Catalyst/Redwood:
- For the presign flow: do you need client-side multipart uploads, or will single-part presigns suffice for your artifacts?
- For the TTL: who should own the lifecycle deletion callback (Vendr deletes, or Catalyst requests a deletion webhook to Redwood for verification)?

I'll attach our presign_runbook_vendr.docx which shows the API endpoints and the expected request/response formats. Happy to jump on a quick call — propose Wed 10–11am PT.

Regards,

Thanks Ari — that's helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- We will ask Catalyst to use single-part presigns for the initial ingest (artifacts are typically <50MB). If in future we need multipart we will re-open the spec.
- For TTL we want Vendr to be the authoritative deleter (simpler for Catalyst). However, Redwood needs a deletion webhook to record the deletion event in our audit log for SOC 2 traceability. Does Vendr support a tenant-level webhook for deletion events?

Jonas (cc) — can you confirm we don't have any internal presign constraints (max TTL) that would conflict with Vendr's default 1h token lifetime? If so, we can either reduce token lifetime or implement a short-lived exchange via Redwood.

If that looks good Ari, please send a short SLA snippet we can attach to the procurement ticket: presign availability, median latency, configured TTL range (7–90 days), and confirmation of immutable manifest fields. Sam — if 14 days is fine, we'll request tenant TTL=14 and request the deletion webhook.

Best,
— Ben

Ben / Ari — quick technical note from infra:

- Redwood has no hard presign lifetime cap beyond 24 hours in our internal tooling, but we recommend <=1h for security. We can accept Vendr's default 1h and rotate tokens on handshake.
- Deletion webhook: we will subscribe to a single tenant webhook endpoint (https://hooks.redwoodinference.com/ingest/deletion) and record deletion events into our internal audit index (SOC2 fields included). We need Vendr to include manifest_sha256 and upload_ts in the webhook payload.
- Multipart: noted that single-part is fine for now. If Catalyst later needs multipart we will revert with throughput/implementation constraints.

Action items:
- Ari: send SLA snippet + confirm webhook payload contains manifest_sha256 & upload_ts.
- Ben/Marissa: update procurement ticket with TTL=14 and the SLA text once received.
- Sam: say the word and we will provision tenant TTL=14 and open the presign exchange.
